proposal.description_long: On August 13, 2020, the Environmental Protection Agency issued final policy amendments to the New Source Performance Standards for the oil and natural gas industry. EPA said the amendments removed the transmission and storage segment from the standards and rescinded methane emissions requirements for production and processing segments. The agency described the rules as simplifying and reducing burdens on industry; environmental groups criticized the rollback because it weakened federal methane controls. The event concerns specific standards adopted under the Clean Air Act, not the later greenhouse-gas endangerment finding discussed in the linked BBC article. The original BBC URL therefore does not support the event and should be replaced with EPA’s rule page or contemporaneous rulemaking materials. This account identifies the provisions changed without adding an unsupported estimate of emissions effects. EPA’s own summary establishes the date and segments affected, while the policy rationale should be attributed to the agency rather than presented as an independent finding.
